name: Willem Bilderdijk
credit: Charles Howard Hodges, portrait of Willem Bilderdijk · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Willem Bilderdijk (1756–1831) was born in Amsterdam and trained as a lawyer at Leiden. Because he refused to swear allegiance to the Batavian Republic he was exiled in 1795, living in Germany and England, and returned to the Netherlands in 1806, where he was court librarian to King Louis Napoleon and later lectured on Dutch history. A scholar of law, language and history as well as a poet, he was a fierce opponent of Enlightenment rationalism and the French Revolution.

His poetry ranges from the classicizing verse of his early years to the religious and historical epics of his later career, among them the unfinished De ondergang der eerste wareld (1820). The didactic poem De ziekte der geleerden (1807), on the maladies of the over-studious, is given here in its first edition. Bilderdijk is regarded as the leading Dutch poet of the Romantic age and a teacher of the writers of the Dutch Réveil.
